For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). 3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

362	CASE OD2-HO-CHANGE-2 (CHANGE, technical): Ashgrove Heights low pressure
363	Setting: Calder Vale Water (fictional) supplies about 410,000 people through 23 district metered areas (DMAs). Each DMA is fed through a metered inlet and is normally kept separate from its neighbours by closed boundary valves. Ashgrove Heights is a hillside DMA of about 6,800 properties. It is fed through a pressure-reducing valve (PRV) on Ridgeway Road. Millbrook Low is the lower-lying DMA that adjoins it to the east. Stage S1 covers evidence available up to 15 September; stage S2 covers evidence gathered from 16 September to 5 October.
364	Presenting request: On 6 October the Director of Network Operations wants an independent diagnosis of the Ashgrove Heights pressure drop before deciding on two requests from the Network Operations Manager: book a rail possession to dig up the trunk main under the rail cutting, and raise the Ashgrove PRV setpoint to 4.8 bar in the meantime.
365	INITIAL EVIDENCE
366	E1 [stage S1] Telemetry summary, critical-point logger PL-AG-03 (telemetry): Critical-point logger PL-AG-03 (Beacon Hill Road, the highest point in Ashgrove Heights DMA). 1–8 Sept: lowest morning-peak pressure (07:00–08:30) 3.1–3.2 bar; overnight 3.7 bar. 9–15 Sept: lowest morning-peak pressure 1.5–1.7 bar every day; overnight 3.0 bar. The company's service reference level is 2.0 bar at peak. Low-pressure customer contacts from Ashgrove: 4 in the whole of August, 38 between 9 and 15 Sept, clustered on Beacon Hill and Ridgeway.
367	E2 [stage S1] Ashgrove Heights DMA inlet meter extract, prepared 15 Sept (telemetry): Ashgrove Heights inlet meter (Ridgeway Road). Minimum night flow (02:00–04:00): 1–8 Sept 6.2–6.4 L/s; 10–15 Sept 14.7–14.9 L/s. One-minute data show a step at 06:40 on 9 Sept: flow rose by 8.6 L/s within four minutes and has stayed up at all hours since. Daily inflow was about 1,950 m³ before and 2,690 m³ after. Analyst comment: the 7–12 Sept heatwave raised daytime demand across the whole system, but no other DMA shows a step in night flow, and Ashgrove's higher night flow continued after temperatures fell on 13 Sept.
368	E3 [stage S1] Network works register, weeks 34–37 (extract) (change-record): 29 Aug — Fenwick Fields development, Ashgrove: the last 12 of 38 new homes connected; development complete. 5 Sept — Ashgrove inlet PRV (Ridgeway Road): annual service by in-house team, pilot valve replaced, 4.0 bar setpoint re-confirmed. 9–27 Sept — Millbrook Low DMA (adjoins Ashgrove to the east): Station Road main renewal, contractor Brannock Civils, permit PTW-2291. Standing condition on all contractor permits: supply-continuity arrangements must be agreed with network control before work starts.
369	E4 [stage S1] Ashgrove inlet PRV controller trend, 1–15 Sept, with asset note (telemetry): Ridgeway Road PRV. Inlet pressure 7.1–7.3 bar. Outlet pressure 3.97–4.03 bar throughout the period, including after the 5 Sept service and after 9 Sept. Valve opening rose from about 31% to about 44% starting at 06:40 on 9 Sept and has stayed there. Asset note on file: under pressure-management policy PM-7, the Ashgrove PRV outlet is capped at 4.2 bar. The cap was set after the 2022 burst cluster, when the outlet was raised to 4.6 bar and the district's 1960s cast-iron mains had 14 bursts in six weeks. Any setting above 4.2 bar requires an asset-risk review.
370	E5 [stage S1] Field note, network technician D. Okafor, 12 Sept (staff-account): 'Asked to rule out water crossing the boundary. GIS shows four pipe connections between Ashgrove and neighbouring DMAs: BV-21 and BV-22 to Millbrook Low, BV-23 to Castle Rise, BV-24 to Northfield. GIS says these are the only mains connections. I found all four and all were shut: I turned each spindle in the closing direction and none moved. I gauged both sides of each valve, and the pressure differences of 0.9–1.6 bar held, so they are sealing. The register agrees. I also asked network control whether any temporary cross-boundary links (including hose or hydrant links) or works cross-feeds had been agreed for Ashgrove or its neighbours; they checked and none were on record. Nothing is crossing at the boundary. My view: look for a burst.'
371	E6 [stage S2] Email, R. Halvorsen, Network Operations Manager, 30 Sept (manager-account): 'The acoustic survey has covered about 70% of Ashgrove mains and found two service-pipe leaks (about 0.4 L/s combined), repaired on 26 Sept. Minimum night flow since then is 14.6 L/s, so the big one is still out there. The only stretch not surveyed is the 1968 trunk main under the rail cutting, where we can't place loggers without a rail possession. Boundary valves were checked and ruled out, and the PRV is fine, so this is a burst under the railway. I'm asking for approval to book a possession and dig. Customer services have already texted every Beacon Hill and Ridgeway customer (16 and 29 Sept) and keep a web notice updated. Meanwhile I propose raising the PRV to 4.8 bar so Beacon Hill customers get above 2 bar at peak.'
372	CATALOGUE (full contents)
373	C1 [stage S1] Ashgrove inlet PRV service record and controller event log, 1–15 Sept - Asset maintenance system (system-record): Work order WO-58812, 5 Sept: annual service, Ridgeway Road PRV. Pilot valve replaced because of seat wear, strainer cleaned, setpoint checked at 4.0 bar against a test gauge, valve back in service 11:20. Controller event log 1–15 Sept: no alarms, no setpoint changes, no manual overrides. One informational event (not alarmed) on 9 Sept at 06:41: 'valve position increase >10% in 5 min'. Technician comment: 'Valve moving smoothly, outlet steady.'

Setting: Calder Vale Water (fictional) supplies about 410,000 people through 23 district metered areas (DMAs). Each DMA is fed through a metered inlet and is normally kept separate from its neighbours by closed boundary valves. Ashgrove Heights is a hillside DMA of about 6,800 properties. It is fed through a pressure-reducing valve (PRV) on Ridgeway Road. Millbrook Low is the lower-lying DMA that adjoins it to the east. Stage S1 covers evidence available up to 15 September; stage S2 covers evidence gathered from 16 September to 5 October.
Presenting request: On 6 October the Director of Network Operations wants an independent diagnosis of the Ashgrove Heights pressure drop before deciding on two requests from the Network Operations Manager: book a rail possession to dig up the trunk main under the rail cutting, and raise the Ashgrove PRV setpoint to 4.8 bar in the meantime.

The company's service reference level is 2.0 bar at peak. Low-pressure customer contacts from Ashgrove: 4 in the whole of August, 38 between 9 and 15 Sept, clustered on Beacon Hill and Ridgeway.
E2 [stage S1] Ashgrove Heights DMA inlet meter extract, prepared 15 Sept (telemetry): Ashgrove Heights inlet meter (Ridgeway Road). One-minute data show a step at 06:40 on 9 Sept: flow rose by 8.6 L/s within four minutes and has stayed up at all hours since. Daily inflow was about 1,950 m³ before and 2,690 m³ after. rulings.explanation: This is the mirror of S02. 'Contradicted' rests on two things: (a) the four mapped valves were physically confirmed sealing, and (b) control had no temporary links on record. (a) covers only mapped pipe connections. (b) is an absence of records, not an observation. E3 shows works in the adjoining district starting on 9 Sept, the same day as the step, under a permit condition about continuity arrangements. That is a positive pointer toward a temporary cross-feed. The key's own S07 rationale accepts that 'not on record' does not mean nothing was arranged, although it relies on S2 evidence (C8) to say so. A careful S1 analyst can therefore read the evidence as counting against H3 ('contradicted'). They can equally read it as leaving H3 live but unestablished ('unknown'). Both readings are defensible.
rulings.fix: Rekey S05 to 'unknown' and apply the same E5 edit as for S02, stating that control's record holds only arrangements already filed and that the PTW-2291 agreement field is filled in only at close-out. With that edit, nothing at S1 physically excludes a temporary non-pipe link, and the same-day adjoining works keep H3 live. 'Unknown' becomes the only defensible answer, and C4/C5 still move it to 'supported' at S2.

rulings.explanation: A4 is not hypothesis-dependent, so 'premature' does not fit. It does not suppress information or disable a control, so 'harmful' does not fit. 'Preferred' would need it to be among the best next actions. E6 records that every Beacon Hill and Ridgeway customer was already texted on 16 and 29 Sept and that a web notice is kept up to date, and A4 is worded as a 'further letter'. It adds little and restores no pressure, while A1 directly fixes the cause. Customers have been below the service level for weeks (E1), so communicating is reasonable and harmless. 'Acceptable' is the only answer that fits.
